leading_positions.synthesis: Six of eight members prefer a single-part prize for optical lattice clocks (Katori and Ye). They share the view that the magic-wavelength idea plus the record-accuracy programme is an original invention, reproduced by independent laboratories at the 1e-18 level, with a compact two-name attribution. They differ in emphasis: Kroll and Mehlig stress Ye's contribution beyond the first demonstration (many-body and spin-correlation physics); Johansson and Kroll want the citation worded around neutral-atom lattice trapping at the magic wavelength; Kroll opposes adding a third name; Lindroth also raises Takamoto, Ludlow, Lemonde and Lisdat as uncredited. Several of these members moved to B007 after reading the openings (Johansson from B044, Mehlig from B025, Olsson from B005), so the shared preference is not an independent count of merit. Every supporter lists B005 or B012 or another candidate as first alternative, and none treats B007 as free of reservations.

Two members prefer a single-part prize for magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, both with MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer, pairing the 2011 flat-band prediction with the 2018 observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity. They share the argument that the phenomenology is reproduced by many groups over about eight years and that the unresolved pairing mechanism should not bar a prize (Eriksson cites high-temperature superconductivity in 1987). They differ on wording: Danielsson would keep the citation to the prediction and observation of the phenomena without implying a settled mechanism. B005 is also the first alternative of Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Olsson and the second alternative of Pearce, so it is the main competitor, but those members do not prefer it in their configuration.

areas_of_agreement: B007 and B005 are the two candidates whose scientific quality all eight members accept as high; the disagreement between them concerns maturity and attribution, not whether the physics is original and important.

Every member who prefers B007 and every member who prefers B005 names the other among their first two alternatives or ranks it near the top, except where B012 or B006 is the stated second alternative (Olsson, Pearce, Eriksson).

All members who address B007 identify the same strongest reservation: possible overlap with the 2005 frequency-comb prize and the 2012 prize for control of single quantum systems, and the pending redefinition of the second.

All members who address B005 identify the same two reservations: the unresolved pairing mechanism of the superconductivity and the absence of Yuan Cao, first author of the 2018 experiments, from the credited names.
B044, B001 and B025 are treated by the members who discuss them as meritorious but not leading this year, for stated reasons of timing, attribution or overlap rather than lack of scientific interest.
scientific_disputes: Whether a prize for lattice clocks is a distinct invention (neutral-atom magic-wavelength trapping, as Johansson, Kroll and Pearce argue) or a continuation of the metrology lineage honoured in 2005 and 2012 (the concern raised by Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson and Eriksson).

Whether an unresolved superconducting pairing mechanism makes B005 premature (Kroll, Lindroth, Johansson, Mehlig, Pearce) or whether robust, widely reproduced phenomenology suffices (Danielsson, Eriksson).
Whether twist-angle disorder and sample dependence in twisted bilayer graphene limit what can be called intrinsic (raised by Eriksson and Olsson as real, but not undermining the core phenomenology).

Whether B001 (anyonic statistics) is a deep conceptual discovery whose 2020 interferometer and collider experiments are sufficiently established (Danielsson) or still contested in interpretation (Lindroth, Olsson, Johansson).

Whether B025 (two-dimensional melting) is distinct enough from the 2016 defect-mediated topological phase recognition, and whether the order of the transition is settled across systems (Mehlig supports it as an idea; Danielsson, Eriksson, Olsson and Pearce doubt the distinctness or maturity).
attribution_disputes: B007: whether Katori and Ye are the correct pair given Takamoto, Ludlow, Lemonde, Lisdat and the PTB, SYRTE and NIST groups. Kroll and Lindroth also stress that Ye's contribution extends beyond the first demonstration, which supports two names; no member proposes a different third laureate.

B005: whether Bistritzer should be included. Danielsson, Eriksson, Lindroth and Pearce list three names; Mehlig and Olsson have proposed MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero only. Cao cannot be named from the supplied credited names, and Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto, Dean, Young and Yazdani are cited as other possible claimants.

Danielsson and Eriksson treat the Cao omission as a recurrent consequence of the three-name limit, not a disqualification, whereas Pearce, Olsson, Mehlig, Kroll and Johansson treat it as a substantive obstacle that favours B007.

B044: four credited names for three places (Blais, Girvin, Schoelkopf, Wallraff); the Opening proposals differ on whether Girvin or Blais is excluded, as Pearce and Johansson's differing triples illustrate.
B001 has six credited names, with Wilczek and Halperin absent, and divided experimental credit (Heiblum, Manfra, Fève, Rosenow).
maturity_disputes: B007: the redefinition of the second has not happened, so some of the claimed impact is prospective; members differ on whether this weakens the case only mildly (Kroll, Pearce, Johansson) or is a reason to wait (raised as an open question by Pearce and Mehlig).

B005: about eight years of replication versus an unsettled mechanism and a fast-moving field; Lindroth and Mehlig suggest the prize would be easier to defend in a few years, while Danielsson and Eriksson describe it as timely.

B044: consecutive recognition of superconducting-circuit work after the 2025 prize is raised by Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce as a timing and balance question; Johansson accepts this although he regards cQED as distinct in content.

B012: Pearce notes that 3-4 sigma source associations may make neutrino astronomy slightly early despite the robust diffuse flux, while Mehlig argues the credit among Halzen, Karle and Yoshida in a large collaboration is arbitrary.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson: directs WACQT at Chalmers and works on superconducting circuits and circuit QED; he proposes recusing or discounting his own view on B044 and, to a lesser extent, B031.

Kroll: spent part of his doctoral period in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, the comb background to the JILA lattice-clock programme where Ye works; no documented link to Katori or Ye and no recusal proposed. He also flags field adjacency to atom interferometry (B043).

Pearce (chair): B012 (IceCube) is in his own field of astroparticle physics, which he flags as field proximity and a possible perception issue; no personal tie to Halzen, Karle or Yoshida is recorded.
Eriksson: flags field proximity to moire and correlated-electron theory as a possible bias toward B005 and asks to be challenged on it.
Lindroth: flags that her atomic-theory background may bias her toward AMO topics; no documented link to Katori or Ye.
Olsson: notes that Johansson is a Chalmers colleague and that she does not treat his B044 opening as independent of institutional context.
questions_for_round2: B007 versus B005 as the single prize: given that all members accept both as high-quality science, does the unresolved pairing mechanism and the omission of Yuan Cao outweigh B005's breadth, or does the pending redefinition of the second and the overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes outweigh B007's clean attribution?

Can a B007 citation be worded so that the neutral-atom magic-wavelength lattice concept and its realisation at the 1e-18 level are what is rewarded, separating it from the comb and ion-clock recognitions, and can members state explicitly whether Takamoto, Ludlow, Lemonde or Lisdat should change their view of a two-name prize?

For B005, which members would change their ranking if Bistritzer is dropped to leave MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero, and which if the citation is limited to the prediction and the observation of the phenomena with no claim on the superconducting mechanism?

Should the committee consider a two-part prize, and if so which second candidate is distinct enough from B007 or B005 (B012, B044, B006) to be paired without blurring attribution? Kroll prefers pairing only with a clearly distinct achievement; Pearce does not favour B043 as a second part.

Is a circuit-QED prize (B044) acceptable in 2026 after the 2025 superconducting-circuit prize, and if it is considered, which of Blais and Girvin takes the theory place, with Johansson's disclosed proximity taken into account?

Should B012 be considered ready given the 3-4 sigma source associations, and can credit among Halzen, Karle and Yoshida be defended within a large collaboration, given Mehlig's and Pearce's differing views?
summary.chair_observation: Six members explicitly prefer a single-part B007 prize and two prefer B005; no other configuration is explicit in the round-1 files, and no member prefers a two-part prize. Several B007 supporters moved there from other first choices after reading the openings, and the supporters themselves attribute their preference to maturity and attribution, not to the count. The central contest is a trade between B005's scale and unresolved mechanism and credit gap and B007's clean attribution and still-prospective payoff. Minority views on B001, B025, B044 and B012 remain on the record with stated reasons.
